headline: Fed's Waller says AI shopping agents need a new kind of authentication
body: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller told Sibos 2026 in Miami on September 29 that agentic commerce shifts what payment authentication has to prove, from a buyer's authority to pay to an agent's authority to pay on that buyer's behalf. Capturing that, he said, "will require new authentication approaches," though he did not prescribe a specific standard.
note: Waller named authentication, liability and fraud as the barriers holding back agent-delegated shopping. Card networks are already filling the gap with their own credentialing schemes, so banks may end up choosing between competing standards before regulators settle on one.
correction: An earlier version said Waller pointed to a new payment object, a machine-readable record of delegated authority. That idea came from coverage of the speech; Waller did not propose a specific standard.
